- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.30) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply “mean reversion” correction: subtract 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.30), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ true values.
